why: Tier-1: CI/observability tooling on a READ path. It adds one dependency-install step to .github/workflows/constraint-readout.yml, a read-only diagnosis producer whose own header already declares it Tier-1 — no order path, no strategy config, no risk caps, no account modes, no src/, no config/, no deploy/, no live-VM runtime file, no persistent table. It cannot change what the trader does. The step exists because that workflow has failed 6 of 6 scheduled runs — its complete history — on a missing PyYAML: check_wip_ceiling.py imports yaml at module scope, the import raised on a bare setup-python runner, the broad except set WIP_CEILING=None, and the self-test gate correctly aborted before --write. Root cause reproduced locally by blocking `import yaml` (identical single FAIL line) with a positive control (yaml present -> ALL PASS). Nothing in the workflow's logic, gating, permissions or schedule is touched; the self-test gate is deliberately left exactly as it is, because it is what stopped a readout diagnosing nothing from reaching the session brief. Self-lands because Tier-1 needs no human OK and routing it through one is the convention pr-landing exists to end; GitHub still merges only on green. The change is a DEPLOY, not an observation — an OPEN-ITEMS row (loud) holds it open until a SCHEDULED run is seen succeeding, and the dependent DUE.md retirement is held on that row rather than on this PR.
